records.text: Ahead of White's pawn, its own file and the files beside it have no enemy pawns. That makes it a passed pawn.
Ahead of Black's pawn, its own file and the files beside it have no enemy pawns. That makes it a passed pawn.
The better move would have left a White pawn with no enemy pawns ahead on its file or the neighboring files. A passed pawn, defined by the missing neighbors ahead.
The better move would have left a Black pawn with no enemy pawns ahead on its file or the neighboring files. A passed pawn, defined by the missing neighbors ahead.
White has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawns live on the neighboring files; pieces may still lend support.
Black has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawns live on the neighboring files; pieces may still lend support.
The better move would leave a White pawn without friendly pawn neighbors on the adjoining files. Isolated, though pieces could still lend support.
The better move would leave a Black pawn without friendly pawn neighbors on the adjoining files. Isolated, though pieces could still lend support.
White's pawns are sharing a file now. Doubled pawns: company, though they cannot defend each other from there.
Black's pawns are sharing a file now. Doubled pawns: company, though they cannot defend each other from there.
The better move would have left White with doubled pawns. Same file, different squares.
The better move would have left Black with doubled pawns. Same file, different squares.
No pawns on this little strip of board. White's rook now has an open file.
No pawns on this little strip of board. Black's rook now has an open file.
The better move would have given White's rook an open file. A file without pawns, though not necessarily without pieces.
The better move would have given Black's rook an open file. A file without pawns, though not necessarily without pieces.
White's rook has a semi-open file now. Friendly pawns are absent from it; enemy pawns are not.
Black's rook has a semi-open file now. Friendly pawns are absent from it; enemy pawns are not.
After the other move, White's rook file would have enemy pawns for company, but none of its own. A semi-open file.
After the other move, Black's rook file would have enemy pawns for company, but none of its own. A semi-open file.
White's knight has found a connection. Previously undefended, it now has a defender.
Black's knight has found a connection. Previously undefended, it now has a defender.
The little web has changed: White's bishop now has a defender where it had none.
The little web has changed: Black's bishop now has a defender where it had none.
White's rook is no longer without support. It has gained a defender.
Black's rook is no longer without support. It has gained a defender.
Even a queen can use company. White's queen, previously undefended, now has a defender.
Even a queen can use company. Black's queen, previously undefended, now has a defender.
The better move would have woven in some support for White's undefended knight. It would have had a defender.
The better move would have woven in some support for Black's undefended knight. It would have had a defender.
Another move would have connected White's bishop to a defender. It had none before.
Another move would have connected Black's bishop to a defender. It had none before.
The better move would have brought support to White's rook, which had no defender.
The better move would have brought support to Black's rook, which had no defender.
With another move, White's queen would have gained a defender. A connection missing before the move.
With another move, Black's queen would have gained a defender. A connection missing before the move.
A connection has come undone. White's knight has lost its last defender.
A connection has come undone. Black's knight has lost its last defender.
White's bishop no longer has anyone defending it. Unsupported isn't the same as lost.
Black's bishop no longer has anyone defending it. Unsupported isn't the same as lost.
The support has fallen away from White's rook. It has no defender now.
The support has fallen away from Black's rook. It has no defender now.
White's queen stands without a defender now. That is a missing connection, not a promise of capture.
Black's queen stands without a defender now. That is a missing connection, not a promise of capture.
Another move would have left White's knight without its last defender. A loose thread to notice in that alternative.
Another move would have left Black's knight without its last defender. A loose thread to notice in that alternative.
The better move would have undone the remaining support for White's bishop. It would have been undefended.
The better move would have undone the remaining support for Black's bishop. It would have been undefended.
With another move, White's rook would have lost its last defender. A different shape to the support around it.
With another move, Black's rook would have lost its last defender. A different shape to the support around it.
The better move would have left White's queen without a defender. Even in that alternative, undefended needn't mean lost.
The better move would have left Black's queen without a defender. Even in that alternative, undefended needn't mean lost.
The knight has left its starting perch for the first time. A little change called development.
There goes the knight, off its original square. Its first outing has begun.
A starting square is empty of its knight now. That's the knight's first move out.
The knight's stay at home is over. It has moved away from its original square for the first time.
The bishop has made its first departure from home. Its starting square is behind it now.
A bishop unfolds from its original square. This is its first move out.
The bishop is no longer where it began the game. That first step away is development.
There is a new spot for the bishop. Until this move, it had stayed on its starting square.
The better move would have sent a knight on its first outing from its starting square.
A different move would have ended the knight's stay at home. Its first move off the original square.
Another branch would have begun with a knight developing: leaving its starting square for the first time.
The knight could have made its first departure from home with the better move. That little beginning was available.
The better move would have unfolded a bishop from its starting square for the first time.
Another move would have begun the bishop's journey away from its original square.
A bishop's first move out was waiting in the alternative. It would have left its starting square behind.
With the better move, the bishop would have ended its stay on its original square. Its first bit of development.
